research.text:
DEEP RESEARCH (browser bot, read the pages itself):
- Grace Hopper invented the first compiler, called A-0, in 1952 while working on the UNIVAC I at Eckert-Mauchly Computer Corporation (https://www.computerhistory.org/tdih/august/16/).
- Before Hopper's compiler, programmers had to write instructions entirely in numeric machine code or cumbersome assembly language (https://www.britannica.com/technology/compiler-computer-science).
- Hopper famously stated that humans are allergic to change and kept telling her that computers could only do arithmetic, not understand English words (https://history.aip.org/history/exhibits/hopper/ftf4.htm).
- The A-0 compiler translated mathematical notation and English-like pseudocode into machine-readable binary code (https://spectrum.ieee.org/grace-hopper-compiler).
- Hopper wanted to make programming accessible to non-mathematicians and business people who didn't know binary (https://www.womenshistory.org/education-resources/biographies/grace-hopper).
- Her pioneering work directly led to the creation of COBOL in 1959, one of the first high-level programming languages (https://www.nsa.gov/portals/75/documents/news-features/declassified-documents/tech-journals/grace-hopper.pdf).
- Hopper earned the nickname "Amazing Grace" and rose to the rank of Rear Admiral in the United States Navy (https://www.defensenc.mil/News/News-Stories/Article/Article/2198083/rear-admiral-grace-m-hopper-amazing-grace/).
- Despite creating the breakthrough tool that spawned all modern software development, Hopper's original A-0 system predated modern keyboard-based coding environments, operating largely via punch cards (https://americanhistory.si.edu/collections/search/object/nmah_334547).

HOOK IDEAS:
1. The person who invented software coding didn't actually write a single line of code.
2. Meet the woman who invented the compiler—even though everyone told her computers could only do math.

beats.image_prompt: Vertical overhead view of a wooden desk with cardboard cutout figures arranged neatly under warm craft studio lighting.
beats.motion: Slow overhead crane shot moving forward across the cardboard craft desk while cutout pieces shift slightly.

beats.narration: People think stop motion requires a massive Hollywood studio budget.
beats.image_prompt: Vertical macro shot of a single tiny cardboard coffee cup model resting on a dark craft paper surface.

beats.narration: Moving ordinary cardboard cutouts frame by frame brings an everyday routine to life on a desk.
beats.image_prompt: Vertical close-up of hands moving a small articulated cardboard figure on a tabletop covered in craft tools.

beats.narration: Adam wakes up at six o'clock every morning for his daily routine.
beats.image_prompt: Vertical still of a small cardboard alarm clock cutout showing six o'clock against a textured background.

beats.narration: Animating on twos requires twelve individual photographs for every single second of video.
beats.image_prompt: Vertical graphic displaying frame count comparisons for stop motion animation.

beats.narration: A one-minute stop-motion sequence uses seven hundred and twenty distinct photos.
beats.image_prompt: Vertical neat grid of tiny paper photo prints spread across a rustic wooden tabletop.

beats.narration: Locking camera exposure and focus prevents visual flickering between individual frames.
beats.image_prompt: Vertical view of a professional digital camera mounted on a sturdy overhead tripod pointing down at a craft workspace.

beats.narration: Every frame tells the story.
beats.image_prompt: Vertical hero shot of a tiny cardboard figure stepping forward into bright morning craft light.
beats.motion: Fast smooth zoom in on the cardboard figure as studio lights flicker and settle.

fact_check.claim: Adam wakes up at six o'clock every morning for his daily routine.
Animating on twos requires twelve individual photographs for every single second of video.
A one-minute stop-motion sequence uses seven hundred and twenty distinct photos.
Locking camera exposure and focus prevents visual flickering between individual frames.

youtube-1.name: youtube-1
youtube-1.summary: Uncut gameplay capture featuring continuous live commentary over The Binding of Isaac. Visuals are raw in-game footage driven by procedural dungeon exploration, fast melee combat, and UI overlays. The production relies on natural game pacing and vocal reactions rather than motion graphics or rapid editing.
youtube-1.image_style: Pixel art 2D roguelike dungeon crawler visuals, dark dingy cellar lighting, muted browns, fleshy reds, and grim cartoon subterranean textures.
youtube-1.pacing: Deliberate and continuous real-time flow dictated by active gameplay rooms and boss battles.
youtube-1.writer_notes: Energetic, conversational British gaming commentary explaining item mechanics and reacting in real-time. Casual, enthusiastic tone with self-deprecating humor during boss encounters.

youtu-2.name: youtu-2
youtu-2.summary: A dark-mode tech explainer combining terminal mockups, UI diagrams, and Wojak meme art. It uses high-contrast neon accents, code animations, and app interface recreations to tell a cautionary engineering story.
youtu-2.image_style: Digital Wojak meme artwork paired with dark-mode software UI mockups, terminal text, and minimalist tech icons on black backgrounds.
youtu-2.pacing: Fast-paced tech narrative driven by dynamic terminal execution, UI updates, and dramatic meme reaction pauses.
youtu-2.writer_notes: Cautionary engineering story structured around a Friday deployment incident. Uses developer humor and relatable technical pitfalls to convey best practices.

upload-3.name: upload-3
upload-3.summary: Minimalist high-contrast tech explainer featuring sleek software UI cards, wireframe schematics, and structured step-by-step workflows. Built on clean monochrome canvases punctuated by glowing red accents and precise micro-typography.
upload-3.image_style: Vector diagrams and sleek UI wireframes on monochrome backgrounds with vivid crimson glows.
upload-3.pacing: Methodical and analytical, structured around six-second informational beats.
upload-3.writer_notes: Authoritative and concise tech tutorial tone. Hooks with industry insider context before breaking complex workflows into numbered steps.

youtu-4.name: youtu-4
youtu-4.summary: A moody cybercrime documentary style blending photorealistic live-action plates with minimalist line-drawn NPC meme faces. Dark-mode tech UI simulations, cloud infrastructure diagrams, and dramatic narrative storytelling drive the investigative pace.
youtu-4.image_style: Cinematic low-key corporate stock photography and nocturnal interiors composited with stylized minimalist vector NPC facial expressions.
youtu-4.pacing: Suspenseful docu-drama pacing balancing deliberate narrative exposition with crisp technical UI walkthroughs.
youtu-4.writer_notes: Forensic true-crime tech breakdown focusing on insider threats and infrastructure vulnerabilities. Balances detailed architectural accuracy with subtle dark humor and ego-driven character dynamics.

upload-5.name: upload-5
upload-5.summary: Satirical digital UI simulation formatted as a remote video conference meeting. High-contrast monochromatic UI framing features desaturated webcam participants disrupted by a surreal red figure.
upload-5.image_style: Dark corporate digital UI mixed with desaturated grayscale webcam headshots and vivid scarlet red humanoid figures.
upload-5.pacing: Deliberate, slow-burn pacing with prolonged static shots mimicking an awkward corporate video call.
upload-5.writer_notes: Dry, deadpan corporate satire. Uses mundane tech workplace tropes escalating into surreal financial and AI commentary.

upload-6.name: upload-6
upload-6.summary: High-contrast neon contour animation against deep black backgrounds, accented by golden-yellow glowing linework. Minimalist cinematic storytelling framed in wide aspect ratios, featuring slow, dramatic character close-ups and low-key lighting.
upload-6.image_style: Golden glowing neon sketch outlines on a pitch-black background, dramatic chiaroscuro cinematic lighting, dark and moody atmosphere.
upload-6.pacing: Deliberate and slow-paced with wide shot duration variance, relying on extended visual holds.
upload-6.writer_notes: Introspective, serious instructional tone. Starts with a relatable creator struggle hook, progressing methodically through dramatic narrative steps.

upload-7.image_style: Cinematic low-key studio lighting, desaturated monochromatic palette with crisp white highlights, macro tech focus, sharp digital texture.
upload-7.name: upload-7
upload-7.pacing: Deliberate and rhythmic with varied shot lengths around three seconds, using quick tech cutaways to maintain momentum.
upload-7.summary: A moody, cinematic desk-setup aesthetic paired with sleek UI motion graphics and sci-fi HUD elements. Desaturated, high-contrast live-action footage of hardware and video editing workflows is accented by minimalist white-line overlays and futuristic interface designs.
upload-7.writer_notes: Focused, process-driven tech narration with an analytical yet inspiring tone. Hook opens on tactile workstation gear before diving into creative progression.

upload-8.image_style: Vibrant commercial 3D beverage packshots with studio rim lighting, vivid red and lime green saturated backgrounds, crisp metallic textures, and clean cutout fruit illustrations.
upload-8.name: upload-8
upload-8.pacing: Layered continuous motion with staggered product slides and text reveals, transitioning into a focused call-to-action hold and logo lockup.
upload-8.summary: High-energy commercial motion graphics featuring bold saturated color blocking, layered diagonal stripes, and smoothly sliding 3D product cans. The aesthetic relies on strong typography, tropical fruit flavor palettes, and retail CTA elements like an animated shopping cart before closing on a centered logo reveal.
upload-8.writer_notes: Punchy retail-oriented copy announcing hydrating fruit drink flavors. Builds anticipation with vibrant flavor names before driving immediate conversion with a clear call to action.

fastedit.name: fastedit
fastedit.summary: A punchy, modern app promo featuring rapid-fire UI mockups against bold, colorful flat backgrounds. Kinetic typography and floating graphical UI chips pop on screen with dynamic speed.
fastedit.image_style: Flat minimalist vector illustrations, crisp mobile UI frames, vivid candy palette, clean digital vector textures.
fastedit.pacing: Hyper-fast, rhythmic montage with quick jump cuts averaging around half a second per shot.
fastedit.writer_notes: Punchy, concise copy focused on ease and speed. Hooks instantly with bold brand value proposition and resolves with a clean logo sign-off.

fastedit2.name: fastedit2
fastedit2.summary: A punchy, modern app showcase combining high-contrast solid backgrounds with clean 3D phone mockups and vector icons. Fast-paced cuts flash bold promotional text and UI screens in vibrant primary and pastel tones.
fastedit2.image_style: Minimalist digital app interface mockups and playful 2D flat illustrations, rendered on bold solid color backdrops with crisp modern lighting.
fastedit2.pacing: Rapid-fire montage with cuts averaging half a second, bursting through app features with dynamic UI animations.
fastedit2.writer_notes: Punchy, benefit-driven copy highlighting effortless finance management. Hooks instantly with bold branding followed by quick feature callouts, ending on a clear brand logo lockup.
